notes:
Summary: Mariner Swift is a mid-size CX platform (SaaS) that wants to reduce live-agent volume by 35% via ticket deflection + an assisted support agent. Strong focus on embeddings and reranking: they plan to index product docs, KB, community forums, and contextual ticket history (~10M documents initial, expected to grow to 50M+).

From initial discovery: CTO (Liam Harrigan) quoted: "We need tight latency — customer flows expect response under 200ms p95 for web chat; enterprise SLAs will need p99 guarantees." Team: product/platform + security heavily involved. Typical query distribution: short retail product Qs (low-latency), troubleshooting steps (longer context).

Technical targets & constraints:
- Index scale target: 10M documents initial, 50M+ roadmap; ~150M vectors expected after embeddings + metadata variants.
- Vector dimensionality expected: 1536 (Open-source embeddings), may evaluate 768/1024 variants for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Latency SLOs: p50 <30ms for vector fetch, p95 <120ms end-to-end for deflection flow, p99 <200ms for primary support flows; reranker step budgeted <=60ms for top-5 final sort.
- Throughput: peak 800 qps for web chat; background batch processing of nightly ticket backfills (200k/day).
- Cost goal: <= $0.003 / interactive query (embeddings+rerank amortized) for self-serve channel; will accept higher for enterprise paid channels.
- Reranking architecture preferred: ANN to retrieve top-100 (recall focus), then a lightweight cross-encoder reranker to re-score top-10-20 and ensure top-5 precision. Interested in Redwood suggestions for quantized re-ranker variants and split routing (dedicated GPU for rerank hot-path).
- Caching: strong interest in prefix/KV caching for repeat queries and session affinity.

Security & compliance:
- Must support SSO/SAML, audit logging, KMS integration.
- Data residency: EU tenant requirement for EU customers; will evaluate Redwood Private/VPC for those segments.
- Retention controls for transcripts and embeddings: 90/365/forever buckets in product roadmap.

POC details so far (2 weeks running):
- Ingest: 1.1M docs (KB + tickets); 1.2M vectors (1536 dims) using open-embedding baseline.
- Retrieval baseline: HNSW index on vector store (third-party) returning top-100 in ~18ms p50, ~70ms p95 for ANN fetch.
- Redwood PoC config: continued experimentation with batching and quantized kernels; initial rerank on a single A100 gave top-5 precision 0.82 on internal eval set.
- Cost snapshot: preliminary estimate $0.0045/query with naive rerank; Redwood Optimize recommendations expected to hit target ~ $0.0028-$0.0032 with dedicated routing and KV caching.

Sales notes / interpersonal:
- Champion: Head of Product, Naomi Park (likes technical detail, responds to perf graphs).
- Security contact: Rajiv Menon (slow; requires SOC2 Type II and SAML proof of concept).
- Quote from Naomi: "If we can show a reliable decrease in live-agent handoffs and keep the latency promises, procurement moves fast."

Next steps (practical):
- Redwood: provide a two-node Dedicated plan quote for PoC with GPU rerank capacity + VPC network diagram.
- Deliver a short-run experiment: cross-encoder quantized reranker (int8) vs fp16 baseline, measure p95/p99 and cost per query.
- Security: provide completed SOC2 + KMS integration notes and EU residency options.
- Internal: Mariner Swift to sign off PoC budget (expected this week).
